title: Client-first prefetch and tool offload PRD (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight PRD sketch for a client-driven prefetch and tool-offload pattern aimed at lowering P95 latency for streaming Hosted API calls that rely on optional heavy tool invocations (external search, long-running API calls, database lookups). It explores an SDK-forward ergonomics model where the client signals intent and supplies fallbacks so the server can opportunistically prefetch or offload expensive steps when latency budgets allow.

Problem statement (user-visible):
- Many embeddings/chat flows require calling external tools (search, bing-like web lookup, 3rd-party APIs) that can blow out end-to-end latencies and degrade streaming experiences.
- Current server-side-only heuristics for tool invocation lead to either: 1) conservative synchronous waits (high latency) or 2) fully async fallbacks that yield partial/incoherent streaming output.
- Clients (mobile/web) have contextual info (cached user state, local index hints) that could be used to decide whether to prefetch or to provide cheaper fallback results. But there is no ergonomic SDK surface to convey that intent with minimal developer friction.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce 95th percentile first-byte latency for tool-using streaming sessions by 30% for priority flows.
- Provide SDK primitives that let developers opt-in with <3 lines of code to a prefetch/offload handshake.
- Define structured output glue so client-supplied fallbacks and server-computed tool outputs reconcile deterministically in the stream.
- Ensure clear observability: per-invocation telemetry showing whether prefetch used, success/fallback, and token/time cost delta.

Non-goals:
- This does not replace server-side routing/fallback policies for quota/cost.
- Not proposing new billing model here; metric hooks will inform future pricing experiments.

High-level approach:
- Introduce an optional, typed SDK flag (callOptions.prefetchIntent) and a small protocol for "prefetch artifacts" the client may attach (lightweight JSON pointers, cached result snapshots, or local embedding IDs).
- Server uses that hint to either prefetch the tool call in the serving runtime or defer to a lower-cost inline heuristic.
- Streaming contract extended with explicit "prefetch-state" frames so the client knows whether the server used the prefetch, initiated a fresh tool call, or fell back to client-supplied data.
- Tool results must be delivered as typed output frames (tool-result-{id}), and the stream must include an idempotency key to allow resume/reconciliation.

SDK ergonomics (proposal):
- JS/TS (example):
  const resp = await redwood.generate({
    prompt: ...,
    callOptions: {
      prefetchIntent: true, // opt-in
      prefetchArtifacts: [{type: 'local-doc', id: 'user-123:note-45', weakSig: 'sha1:...'}],
      onStreamingFrame(frame) { /* handles partials incl tool-result frames */ }
    }
  })
- Minimal primitives: prefetchIntent (bool), prefetchArtifacts (list of typed small pointers), prefetchTTL (ms), prefetchCostBudget (ms or token budget).
- SDK will surface helper to compute weak signatures for local caches; we intentionally avoid uploading full client data by default.

Streaming semantics and output types:
- Extend streaming frame types:
  - prefetch-state: {status: "used|miss|skipped", reason: string} (informational)
  - tool-call-start: {tool: "web-search", call_id: "t-abc"} (signal that a tool invocation has begun)
  - tool-result:<call_id>: typed result payload (may be chunked)
  - tool-result-commit:<call_id>: finalization frame (idempotent)
  - fallback-indicator: {source: "client|server-heuristic", summary: string}
- Client receives frames interleaved with tokens; when a tool-result-commit arrives the runtime can patch later tokens or emit correction tokens marked as "correction" to preserve streaming UX without silent content drift.
- Replay/resume contract: all tool frames include a stable call_id and an idempotency key so clients that reconnect can ask server to resume from last-known commit.

Tool offload vs prefetch decisioning (server-side):
- If prefetchIntent + artifact signature matches cheap-cache hit → use cached artifact (no tool).
- If prefetchIntent and latency budget > toolEstimate → server initiates tool call in parallel to model generation; include tool-result frames when available.
- Otherwise server emits fallback-indicator and proceeds with lower-fidelity generation path.
- Administrative flags: product teams can set policy by route/model: force-prefetch, disallow-prefetch, prefer-fallback.

Structured output reconciliation rules:
- Each tool-result is CRDT-like: small typed blocks with a required summary field and optional authoritative flag. The model may incorporate the tool-result or indicate it ignored the result (explicit ignore frame).
- To reduce surprise, corrections must be explicit: model tokens that overwrite earlier narrative MUST be wrapped by a "correction" meta-frame with before/after snippets. SDKs will provide utilities to render corrections gracefully.

Observability and instrumentation:
- New telemetry events: prefetch.requested, prefetch.used, toolcall.started, toolcall.latency, toolcall.success, toolcall.fallback, stream.correction.count.
- Surface in Console: per-route breakdown of prefetch hit-rate, cost delta (tokens/latency) and top fallback reasons.
- Link traces to underlying tool backends (search cluster, external APIs) for outage debugging.

Failure modes and safety:
- If tool results contain PII or unsafe content, server must sanitize and attach provenance metadata.
- Client-supplied artifacts are weak-signed pointers only; full data upload is opt-in via explicit API and flagged in telemetry.
- Inconsistency handling: when correction frames are large, SDK provides compact diff display (default) and full-raw fallback for developer debugging.

Developer experience and migration path:
- Default SDK behavior: prefetchIntent=false (opt-in).
- Provide a small migration guide: 1) Add callOptions.prefetchIntent=true 2) Pass 1-2 prefetchArtifacts from local cache 3) Test flows while watching Console metrics.
- Quickstart snippet + playground route in sandbox to demonstrate end-to-end.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Billing implications: should prefetch attempts (even cache misses) incur tool invocation charges? proposal: only charge for actual tool executions; prefetch cache checks are free. Needs Finance sync.
- Backward compatibility: how many SDK versions do we support? propose v-next only and a lightweight server toggle to enable/disable per-customer.
- How to model compound tool graphs (fanout to many tools)? initial scope: single tool per call; follow-ups can generalize.

Next steps (short timeline):
- Build prototype in serving runtime to emit prefetch-state frames (ENG: serving-runtime team) — 2 sprints (REINF-2145).
- Add JS SDK primitives + tests + sandbox route (ENG: developer-experience) — 1 sprint.
- Instrument telemetry + Console panel (ENG: console-and-rollouts + observability) — 1 sprint.
- Run canary on low-traffic hosted routes for 2 weeks, measure P95 impact, iterate.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a short security FAQ for client-artifact usage (Priya)
- Confirm GitHub PR for SDK changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/142 (work in progress)
- Slack thread draft: #prod-hosted-api "prefetch sketch"; capture feedback before internal review.

References and related work:
- internal: hosted-api/compact-session-protocol (see Console), streaming-tool-handshake-observability-checklist
- prototype: linear/REINF-2145-prefetch-prototype
- GH: github.com/redwood-inference/rein-runtime/pull/89 (prefetch-state frame)

This doc is intentionally a sketch — lots of behavioral edges left. Priority now is building minimal end-to-end prototype so product can evaluate latency wins and developer ergonomics.
